topic.title: STAR story anatomy — conflict-with-a-colleague story
topic.concept: A STAR answer front-loads just enough context, spends most of the time on YOUR actions, and lands on a quantified result plus a lesson — 90 seconds total, not five minutes.
points: Budget: Situation+Task ~20% (2-3 sentences), Action ~60% with 'I' not 'we', Result ~20% quantified.
Quantify the result even approximately: 'cut deploy failures from weekly to ~1/quarter' beats 'it improved'.
Conflict stories need a named disagreement, the resolution mechanism (data, prototype, escalation criteria), and what changed in YOUR behavior after.
Prepare 6-8 stories mapped to competencies (conflict, failure, ambiguity, leadership, deadline) — each retellable in 3 depths: 30s, 90s, 5min.
Follow-up-proof: interviewers ask 'what would you do differently?' — have a real answer, not 'nothing'.
topic.angle: 'Tell me about a disagreement with a teammate.' Weak answers blame or stay vague; strong answers show a decision mechanism (we agreed to benchmark both) and a measured outcome.
